 ORDER

This is the second bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No.60/2023 registered at Police Station - Avadhpuri, District - Raisen (M.P.) for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 354(D), 305,
376(3) of the Indian Penal Code and under Section 11(ii)/12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Applicant is in detention since 30.03.2023.

His first application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 12.05.2023 passed in M.Cr.C.No.20143/2023.
3.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is in jail since 30.03.2023.
He has falsely been implicated in this case.
There is no direct or indirect evidence against the applicant to make out the prima facie case under Section 305 and 376(3) of IPC.

Initially, police had filed charge sheet under Section 363, 354 D(ii) and 305 of IPC, r/w Section 11(iv)/12 of POCSO Act, thereafter at later stage, the Court framed charge under Section 376(3) of IPC and 3 and 4 of POCSO Act.
He invited attention of this Court to the statement of the father, mother and brother of the deceased and submitted that there are many contradictions in their statements.
Their statements are not reliable.
He further submitted that there is no evidence against the applicant.

On the date of incident,
deceased had not gone to coaching but went with the applicant so her brother scold her and thereafter the deceased committed suicide.
Applicant and the deceased were just friends.

They met Yash Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45469480/
1 through the social media and just because they went together, applicant has been made accused.

entities.text: Yash Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Entire case is an afterthought story.
There is nothing objectionable on CCTV footage.
DNA report also does not supports the prosecution case.
Charge sheet has been filed.
Applicant has no criminal antecedents.
Trial is not yet completed.
Therefore, it has been prayed that the applicant may be released on bail.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for State as well as learned counsel for the objector have vehemently opposed the prayer for grant of bail to the applicant and submitted that age of the deceased is 11 to 13 years.
In CCTV footage, it is found that deceased was with present applicant on the date of incident.
Police has recovered their whatsapp chats also.
In DNA report it is mentioned that from the clothes of the deceased, very low uninterpretable Y- DNA profile has been found but in FSL report human sperm was found from the clothes of the deceased.
5. Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, age of the deceased and seriousness of the offence, I am not inclined to grant bail to the applicant.
Hence, the application is dismissed.
